title: Do two sentences mean the same?
intro: You will see two sentences. Say whether Sentence 2 means the same as Sentence 1.
Answer from the words only. Use 'unsure' if you really cannot decide.

help.text: Same if a listener would understand the same thing from both. Different if the listener would understand something else, even if the wording is close.
Contractions (I am / I'm), word order that does not change who does what, and similar style differences do not make a difference.

q1.title: Same meaning?
q1.text: Do the two sentences tell the listener the same thing: who does what to whom, whether it is so or not, when it happens, how sure the speaker is, and whether it is a statement, a question or a request? Small differences in wording or style do not count.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: I will go to the shop.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: I will not go to the shop.

practice.fb: The second sentence says the opposite (not going), so they are different.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: It is raining now.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: It's raining now.

practice.fb: Only the contraction differs, so they mean the same.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: We plan a picnic in the park on Sunday.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: We refuse to plan a picnic in the park on Sunday.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: My friend is not sharing the holiday photos.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: My friend does not share the holiday photos.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: I'm sure we will go for a dog walk.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: I am sure we will go for a dog walk.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: Could you please turn down the music in the car?

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: Please lower the music in the car.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: Did they call their brother in the past?

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: I am asking whether they called their brother in the past.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: The cashier gives me a receipt.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: No cashier gives me a receipt.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: I refuse to carry the inhaler.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: I carry the inhaler.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: No one respects the guest.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: Yes, they respect the guest.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: They fail to tell that the picnic is included.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: They tell that the picnic is included.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: They are going to travel to the park by taxi later.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: They will take a taxi to the park later.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: I tasted the soup.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: I am tasting the soup now.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: The neighbors mentioned that they are planning a picnic.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: They are planning a picnic.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: I invite Sam to the picnic this weekend.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: I refuse to invite Sam to the picnic this weekend.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: You cooked the vegetable soup for dinner.

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: The vegetable soup was cooked by you for dinner.

blocks.label: Sentence 1
blocks.text: Did the rent payment leave my account [PAST]?

blocks.label: Sentence 2
blocks.text: I am asking whether the rent payment left my account.
